gbm_population_evidence.quote: Patients with a histologically confirmed or suspected high-grade glioma (HGG) by MRI.

candidate_evidence.quote: On Day 7, participants will begin combination antiretroviral therapy (ART) consisting of Abacavir, Lamivudine, and dose escalation/de-escalation of Ritonavir (RTV), to determine the recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D) of Ritonavir.
Synergistic Treatment With Antiretrovirals and Laser Interstitial Thermal thErapy (STARLITE) for Unresectable High-Grade Gliomas

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: in patients with newly diagnosed high-grade glioma(s) that cannot be removed surgically

role_evidence.quote: Participants will take one 600mg tablet of Abacavir orally once daily, as part of combination antiretroviral therapy (ART).
Participants will take one 300mg tablet of Lamivudine orally once daily, as part of combination antiretroviral therapy (ART)
Participants will take one tablet of Ritonavir (RTV) orally twice daily, as part of combination antiretroviral therapy (ART), at one of the following dose levels:
to determine the recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D) of Ritonavir

agents.drug_class_hint: HIV protease inhibitor (antiretroviral); dose-escalated up to 600 mg twice daily

role_evidence.quote: Participants will take Temozolomide (TMZ) via capsule orally, during and after focal radiotherapy, as part of standard of care adjuvant therapy.

coder_notes: Fails S5: only 'high-grade glioma' in conditions and eligibility; glioblastoma not named anywhere. Agents coded in full anyway. Ritonavir is dose-escalated as part of the ART regimen (not described as a PK booster), so coded as a candidate rather than delivery_enabling. No mechanism stated beyond 'Synergistic Treatment With Antiretrovirals and Laser Interstitial Thermal thErapy' in the title. LITT is a procedure paired with ART; the record does not state LITT activates or delivers the antiretrovirals, so device_dependent false (adjudicator may consider R4). HLA-B*5701 exclusion is a germline safety marker, not recorded as a biomarker. Single-group sequential cohorts (Part 1, Part 2) both experimental; neither acts as control.
